source_text: Ceterum duo ista quae iungis, liberum et non liberum, id est liberum et captivum, illi quidem rei de qua agitur, convenire non possunt; tibi vero stultitiam singularem, impudentiam novam, impietatem veterem inesse testantur.
pass_a_gloss: For the rest these two which you join, free and not free, that is free and captive, cannot indeed fit that thing about which it is treated; but they testify that there is in you a singular stupidity, a new shamelessness, an old impiety.

lemmas.lexica: LS liber=free; Blaise unde liberum est abstinere

pass_b_english: These two things you join together, free and not free, that is, free and captive, cannot both fit the thing under discussion. But they testify that you possess extraordinary foolishness, a new shamelessness, and an old impiety.

choices.why: Freedom to abstain is required for will and sin.
LS pietas: duty to God/kin. Julian pairs it with ratio as catholic fortification.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
